The budget resolution does not address any issues related to Medicaid. However, Medicaid is in need of reform, as it contributes significantly to our nation's deficit and accounts for the highest number of fraudulent government payments. 
https://t.co/YxAZgTQ0kv

🚨 As we assess the state of Medicaid, we find that roughly one in every four dollars spent is improper, with more than 80% of these payments stemming from eligibility errors. 

My bill, the Ensuring Medicaid Eligibility Act will make sure that those who truly need it can continue to access the care they depend on.
https://t.co/egDvUBueLF

I promised to bring more of Utah to D.C., and my bill—the Healthy Lunch for Healthy Kids Act—does just that by removing ultraprocessed foods from schools and replacing them with nutritious meals that support kids' growth, development, and success.
https://t.co/PYJQrJC9Dd

I had an interesting discussion with @RegulatingAI about the evolving role of artificial intelligence in healthcare.
https://t.co/1mPikMd1lr

I had the pleasure of meeting with representatives from the Utah Hospital Association, including President Francis Gibson and Vice President Dave Gessel. We discussed a range of important topics, from Medicaid to the unique challenges facing rural healthcare. It’s always a pleasure to return to my roots and talk medicine again!

I had a great time as acting Chairman of the Science, Space, and Technology committee today where we discussed United Staes leadership in quantum technology. As a physician, I’m particularly interested to see how quantum computing will accelerate advances in healthcare. https://t.co/NTcH2ltfS1

We had a Utah Legislature reunion here in Washington, discussing the physical and mental health of Utahns. Always great to see you, Representative Steve Elison and Senator Luz Escamilla! https://t.co/SLtmUVBM9p

I had a great conversation with Utah Insurance Commissioner, Jon Pike, about empowering states through insurance legislation and the best ways to protect Utahns. I am grateful for his insights and leadership as we work toward stronger and smarter protections for our communities. https://t.co/rc6krmSge0

I had a great conversation on the Breaking Battlegrounds podcast about my new bill, which ensures that Medicaid serves those it was originally intended to help.
https://t.co/AwLANIhLZk

There are 7.6 million people on Medicaid who should not be. Having worked with families that rely on Medicaid for over 20 years, it is my priority during this reconciliation process to preserve the program and ensure it is structured for long-term sustainability. https://t.co/4UzJWFKjFe

I voted to advance President Trump’s One Big Beautiful bill—a commonsense package that delivers real results by: 

 ✅ Prioritizing American families and businesses 

✅Strengthening SNAP work requirements 

✅Eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse in Medicaid

✅ Bolstering U.S. border security and our economy 

✅ Unleashing American energy dominance

Fixing critical programs like Medicaid and SNAP is one of the reasons I ran for Congress. I’m proud that President Trump’s Big Beautiful Bill includes key reforms from my Ensuring Medicaid Eligibility Act and Let’s Get to Work Act to make sure support reaches those who truly need it.

🚨I introduced the Safe Prescribing Through Reporting Act of 2025 to help doctors avoid dangerous drug interactions while balancing privacy with safety.

For the best patient outcomes, providers should have the full picture when prescribing.
https://t.co/2kgWFxp2uq

Biotech plays a vital role in Utah’s economic growth, public health innovation, and scientific advancement. It is crucial that we eliminate barriers hindering America’s biotech innovation to maintain a competitive edge against adversaries such as the CCP. https://t.co/EtgZIGvLpf

I support the USDA’s decision to grant Utah a waiver to remove soda from SNAP benefits. Taxpayer dollars shouldn’t fund unhealthy foods—whether in school lunches or SNAP. This is a smart step for better health and respects Utah’s right to local control.

https://t.co/OVktxcHNfv
This is a massive pro-life victory. The Supreme Court just cleared the way for states to stop sending Medicaid funds to Planned Parenthood. Taxpayers should never be forced to fund abortion.

Yesterday I took the House floor to make one thing clear:
Medicaid must be preserved for those who truly need it by protecting the vulnerable and rooting out fraud, waste, and abuse.

I’m grateful that key provisions from my Ensuring Medicaid Eligibility Act of 2025 were secured in this landmark legislation—helping ensure support reaches those who qualify and rely on it.

The One Big Beautiful Bill proves we don’t have to choose. We can protect those in need and stop the waste.

Thank you to all 15,000+ who tuned in to my telephone town hall tonight. We covered the Epstein files, Medicaid reform, support for our veterans, and more. Utahns want common sense, accountability, and transparency. I’m taking that message back to Washington. https://t.co/fImJluWjmc

This avoidable government shutdown is impacting 1.3 million active-duty service members, delaying checks for 1.9 million civilian employees, and leaving over 100,000 federal law-enforcement officers working without pay. It halts small-business loans and risks nutrition assistance for women and children.

The economic toll is severe: each week a shutdown drags on, it costs the nation about $15 billion in GDP and could put 43,000 Americans out of work if it lasts a month.

All while the latest proposal prioritizes funding new healthcare coverage for illegal immigrants.

We need to reopen the government and get back to legislating responsibly.

Spent the morning working in the district, meeting with Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Utah in Sandy. We got an inside look at their facility and had a productive conversation on the incredible work they’re doing. 

Always great to connect with local providers and hear directly from those serving Utah families. Their perspective is invaluable as I continue to advocate for my constituents in Washington.

Great morning touring the Huntsman Cancer Institute. I was privileged to meet with their CEO and executive leadership team for an up close look at the work they are doing. 

Two- thirds of @huntsmancancer patients live in Utah. I am thankful for their dedication to lifesaving research and care. In just over 25 years, HCI has redefined the fight against cancer—from understanding and prevention, to early detection, treatment, and improved survival rates.

For the past ten months in Congress, I’ve been having conversations to deliver meaningful reform that addresses both healthcare affordability and our national debt. Senate Democrats must reopen the government so we can continue these conversations.

Obamacare promised affordability, but premiums keep rising, fraud has exploded, and taxpayers pay the price while insurers cash in. 

Instead of pouring billions into a broken system, we should restore accountability, cap subsidies, and expand real solutions like HSAs, competition, and reforms that actually lower costs.

Americans deserve healthcare that’s affordable because it is affordable, not because Washington hides the bill.

I am incredibly thankful for the opportunity to represent the wonderful people of Utah’s Third Congressional District. Thanksgiving reminds us to reflect on the blessings in our lives. I am thankful for my health, family, friends, and the freedoms we share as Americans.

To everyone gathering today, I wish you a day filled with warmth, great food, and cherished memories.

There’s a nationwide shortage in our healthcare workforce.

As a family doctor, I’ve seen firsthand the strain this puts on Utah’s hospitals, clinics, and families. Strong patient care depends on having enough trained professionals.

That’s why I introduced the Fast Track Health Care Apprenticeship Act, a necessary step to streamline training pathways and strengthen our workforce.
